findings.problem: Not fixed. The subject line "Last chance to detox with The Steep Club!" uses fake urgency: "last chance" is a banned phrase (claim rule 2). It also makes a detox claim (claim rule 1).
findings.fix: Change it to something like "Subject: Take a moment with The Steep Club".

findings.problem: Not fixed. The preview line says "Our tea flushes out toxins," which is a detox claim (claim rule 1). "Hurry, this offer won't last" is fake urgency (claim rule 2) and uses "hurry" from the words-we-avoid list. There is no dated offer in the email to back it up.
findings.fix: Use a warm, honest preview, e.g. "Preview: A small-batch cup, picked and tasted by us. Come and see what's brewing."

findings.problem: Partly fixed. The detox, cleanse and seven-day claims are gone, but the line still opens with "This is your last chance." That is fake urgency (claim rule 2) and a banned phrase.
findings.fix: Delete "This is your last chance." and keep the rest, e.g. "Our green tea is one we picked and tasted ourselves. Brew a cup and take a moment."

findings.problem: Not fixed. There is a second link, "[Read our detox guide](https://kettlebird.example/detox-guide)". The email rules allow exactly one link (to /steep-club). The link text and URL also push a detox claim (claim rule 1).
findings.fix: Delete line 10 completely. Keep only the single Steep Club button link.

findings.problem: Not fixed. The button text "Join now" is pushier than our voice (warm, unhurried, never pushy) and leans toward "act now" urgency.
findings.fix: Use softer wording, e.g. "[Discover The Steep Club](https://kettlebird.example/steep-club)".
